scope: Update consumer ('agentdocker desktop update') verification on 2026-09-11: unit tests, lint and the offline update smoke against a locally packaged release under a disposable prefix. Online verification against a published updates.json awaits the first release that ships one.

source.note: updater committed on top of c9677ab; the tree also carried no other uncommitted sources at smoke time

unit_tests.agentdocker: 152 passed, 2 ignored (includes update: version ordering, target selection incl. universal Mac fallback, preview/file feeds need --local-preview, curl pinned to https/redirect/size/time bounds, checksum/size/name validation, archive entry audit)
unit_tests.agentdocker-ui: 102 passed (includes panel update-check/update operations and apply pin through an update preview)

steps: file feed refused without local preview
check reports no update for the running version and downloads nothing
check sees the advertised newer version
payload whose metadata disagrees with the feed is refused before install
tampered checksum refused; no partial file, no extraction
download, verify, extract and preview of the newer release
apply produced a managed installation of the advertised version
second check finds nothing newer than the installed version

guards: feed <= 128 KiB read into scratch; a --check writes nothing under the prefix
archive size from the feed enforced by --max-filesize, then bytes and SHA-256 verified; .part removed on mismatch
archive entries listed and audited before extraction: absolute, '.'/'..', backslash, outside payload/__MACOSX, link or special entries refused

payload inspected by the installer (links, target, checksums, codesign, Gatekeeper unless --local-preview) and must equal the feed's version/source/schema/target and be newer than the installed or running version
install pins --expect-release/--expect-current; schema downgrade refused; rejected payload/archive removed
daemon queried without autostart for live agents; never restarted
not_covered: a real https feed and GitHub redirect
Linux tar path (audited by the same rules, not exercised here)
